name: Dr. Dre
hook: N.W.A's main producer left the group in 1991 and built G-funk, an entire West Coast sound, largely out of George Clinton's catalogue.

blurb.age7: Dr. Dre was a producer in the rap group N.W.A. After he left, he made his own albums built around slow, funky beats, and started a record label that found stars like Eminem.
blurb.age13: Andre Young, known as Dr. Dre, was N.W.A's main producer. He left the group in 1991 and co-founded Death Row Records with Suge Knight. His 1992 solo album 'The Chronic' pioneered G-funk, a slower, synth-and-funk-sample-heavy style built heavily on George Clinton and Parliament-Funkadelic's music, including George Clinton's own solo hit 'Atomic Dog'. Dre later founded Aftermath Entertainment in 1996 and signed Eminem in 1998. In 2006 he co-founded Beats Electronics, sold to Apple in 2014.
blurb.adult: 'The Chronic' (1992) is the record that made G-funk the dominant West Coast sound of the early-to-mid 1990s, built on dense, mostly uncredited-at-release P-Funk sampling; 'Fuck Wit Dre Day' alone draws on multiple Parliament-Funkadelic and George Clinton recordings, including the 'Atomic Dog' chant. Dre's later career, Aftermath, Eminem, and Beats Electronics, sits outside this map's scope. Also part of the record: Dre pleaded no contest in 1991 to assaulting television host Dee Barnes, was sentenced to probation, and a related civil suit was settled; he has since acknowledged the assault, first documented on this map at N.W.A's own entry.
